# Definition-of-Done Checklist: Shop Desk

**Purpose**: Validate that the Shop Desk requirements are complete, unambiguous, consistent, and demonstrable before implementation starts
**Created**: 2026-09-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/sp.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements. Each item tests the *requirements*, not the implementation.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are all three model-configuration levels (process, agent, single-run) named with the call site that owns each one? [Completeness, Spec §FR-1]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the behaviour change to be observed when the process default is removed stated precisely enough to be a pass/fail check? [Completeness, Spec §FR-1]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the fields of the shop context object enumerated, and is "never in prompt text" expressed as a verifiable condition? [Completeness, Spec §FR-2]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the set of tools available per customer tier specified, including which tool is statically disabled? [Completeness, Spec §FR-7]
- [x] CHK005 Are the reasons that may trigger escalation enumerated as a closed set of values? [Completeness, Spec §FR-10] — closed set added to FR-10
- [ ] CHK006 Is the cost line's required content (turns, tokens, serving model, path type) itemised? [Completeness, Spec §FR-11]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the interface's session-to-basket ownership rule stated, and is per-session isolation specified for more than one concurrent session? [Completeness, Spec §FR-12]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK008 Is "one model call" for the fast path quantified precisely enough to be counted from a trace? [Clarity, Spec §FR-3]
- [ ] CHK009 Is "the model never sees the result" stated as an observable property rather than an intention? [Clarity, Spec §FR-3]
- [ ] CHK010 Is "outside shop hours" defined with opening hours as configuration and a simulated clock for demonstration? [Clarity, Spec §FR-4]
- [ ] CHK011 Is "recomputed rather than trusted" specified as an algorithm-free but checkable rule (total derived from line items)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-5]
- [ ] CHK012 Is "quotes a price or SKU not in the catalogue" defined as a comparison against catalogue data, with the refusal's user-visible outcome stated? [Clarity, Spec §FR-6]
- [ ] CHK013 Is "answers with a figure rather than a paragraph" measurable for the pricing specialist's response? [Clarity, Spec §FR-8]
- [ ] CHK014 Is "demonstrable with identity comparisons" defined for what the clones share versus own? [Clarity, Spec §FR-9]
- [ ] CHK015 Is the turn ceiling stated as a number? (Resolved: 10 turns.) [Clarity, Spec §FR-8]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK016 Do the cost-line requirements (§FR-11) agree with the fast-path requirement (§FR-3) on how a fast-path turn is identified? [Consistency]
- [ ] CHK017 Does the guardrail requirement (§FR-6) agree with the source-of-truth requirement (§NFR-3) and the catalogue-only entity definition? [Consistency]
- [ ] CHK018 Does the clone requirement (§FR-9) agree with the three-level model configuration (§FR-1) without a clone restating an inherited model? [Consistency]
- [ ] CHK019 Does the trimming rule (§FR-12) agree with the requirement that no session shares a basket, and with escalation's trimmed history (§FR-10)? [Consistency]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK020 Can each of SC-001…SC-008 be evaluated without reading source code? [Measurability]
- [ ] CHK021 Is SC-002 ("100% of quoted prices trace to the catalogue") phrased so the mid-conversation catalogue edit is a demonstrable check? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK022 Is SC-005's "eleven turns still remembers the order under discussion" specific about what counts as remembering? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-005]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK023 Are primary, alternate (tier-gated tools), exception (ceiling hit, guardrail refusal) and recovery (handoff) flows each represented in the acceptance scenarios? [Coverage]
- [ ] CHK024 Is the partial-failure path specified for a tool that meets unusable data (§NFR-4) and does it map to a user-visible message? [Coverage]
- [x] CHK025 Is the escalation scenario defined for all three stated triggers (out of catalogue, unhappy customer, ceiling reached)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-10] — five triggers now closed in FR-10

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK026 Are the concurrent-session and last-unit-of-stock cases addressed by a stated rule rather than left open? [Edge Case] — §FR-6 read-time stock with no implied reservation; §FR-12 per-session baskets
- [x] CHK027 Is the mid-conversation catalogue change (price edited or item removed) covered by an explicit requirement? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-6] — FR-6 now covers removal and re-read
- [x] CHK028 Is the malformed-missing-catalogue startup case assigned an owner requirement (§NFR-1 or §NFR-4) and an expected behaviour? [Edge Case] — assigned to §NFR-4
- [x] CHK029 Is a request for more units than stock addressed, with a stated customer-visible outcome? [Edge Case] — added to §FR-5

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK030 Is the startup failure on a missing secret specified as one readable sentence, distinct from a stack trace? [Completeness, Spec §NFR-1]
- [ ] CHK031 Is "every override is justified in the plan" a checkable obligation on the planning artifact? [Traceability, Spec §NFR-2]
- [ ] CHK032 Is "a tool that raises is a defect" stated with the required tool behaviour (a usable sentence) so it can be tested? [Clarity, Spec §NFR-4]
- [ ] CHK033 Is the provenance requirement (§NFR-5) expressed as an ordering claim that can be read from version history? [Measurability, Spec §NFR-5]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK034 Are the assumptions (single shop, two tiers, configuration-driven hours, file-read catalogue) documented and consistent with the requirements that rely on them? [Assumption]
- [ ] CHK035 Is the deliberate exclusion of order persistence stated in a way that does not conflict with "what did I order last week" appearing anywhere else? [Assumption, Gap]
- [ ] CHK036 Are the three deliberate non-goals recorded with enough precision that scope creep can be rejected by reference? [Completeness]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK037 Is any remaining vague adjective ("sensibly", "polite", "useful") given a concrete observable outcome? [Ambiguity]
- [ ] CHK038 Is it stated what the specialist still needs from the trimmed history, so "useful" is not left to interpretation? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-10]
- [ ] CHK039 Is the trace requirement (§FR-13) specific about how the most expensive turn is identified from the trace? [Clarity, Spec §FR-13]

## Notes

- Check items off as completed: `[x]`
- Items marked `[Gap]` identify requirements that must be written before `/sp.plan`, or explicitly
  deferred with a rationale recorded in the plan.
- Items referencing resolved clarifications (CHK015) are satisfied by the Clarifications section.

## Evidence (2026-09-28)

Commands run in the repository root against the built Desk. `pytest -q` → **37 passed**.

| Guide check | Command | Observed result |
|---|---|---|
| Spec preceded code | `git log --oneline` | `ec9c858` init → `1197de8` constitution → `1da7cb3` spec → `ee9f0e8` clarify/checklist → `6442603` plan/ADRs → `833cb23` tasks; first source commit comes after all six |
| Three configuration levels present | `python -c "from shopdesk.agents import show_clone_identity; ..."` | `models: {desk: None, pricing: None, escalation: None, order: 'gpt-5-mini'}`; global via `OPENAI_DEFAULT_MODEL` in `.env`; run level in `pricing.re_quote_impl` |
| Context never in the prompt | `python scripts/demo_checks.py grep-checks` | PASS — no prompt string carries `customer_id`; no tool schema exposes a context parameter |
| Fast path costs one call | `python scripts/demo_checks.py price-call-count` | SKIP offline — needs a live `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the turn is tagged `fast_path` in the cost line |
| Order total recomputed | `python scripts/demo_checks.py total-mismatch` | PASS — stated 1000 vs recomputed 12600 reported |
| Prices come from the file | `python scripts/demo_checks.py catalogue-edit` | PASS — answer passes, then trips with offending `[4200.0]` after the catalogue price changes |
| Tools differ by tier | `python scripts/demo_checks.py tools-by-tier` | PASS — walk-in 4 tools, regular 5; `seasonal_offer` in neither |
| Escalation carries a typed reason | `python scripts/demo_checks.py escalation` | PASS — reason is a value from the closed set |
| History trimmed on transfer | `python scripts/demo_checks.py escalation` / `trim` | PASS — 7 items → 4 transferred (3 tool items removed); 20 → 13 on the session trim |
| Ten turns and still coherent | `chainlit run chainlit_app.py` | PENDING — needs a live `OPENAI_API_KEY`; per-session context and the trim rule are implemented and tested offline |

**Not yet verified without a key**: SC-001's live call counts, SC-005's eleven-turn recall, and
SC-007's trace contents. Each is implemented (`shopdesk/fastpath.py`, `shopdesk/runner.py`,
`shopdesk/tracing.py`) and has an offline test where one is possible.
